matches.q: What is a fabric treated to be easily washable and to require no ironing called?
matches.d: A fabric treated to be easily washable and to require no ironing.

matches.q: A French “mixed motowasher” demonstrated in 1925 could wash clothing and what other household items?
matches.d: The machine combined laundry and dishwashing functions without requiring special plumbing.

candidates.q: What unexpected genetic cargo has the flowering shrub Amborella accumulated inside its mitochondria?
candidates.a: DNA from other kinds of plants
candidates.d: Its mitochondrial genome contains large amounts of foreign DNA, including material from mosses and green algae. These transfers crossed branches of the plant family tree rather than following ordinary parent-to-offspring inheritance.

matches.q: Which plant can range from a 30-centimetre (12 in) shrub to a 25-metre (82 ft) tree?
matches.d: Persoonia media is a species of flowering plant in the family Proteaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia.

matches.q: The New Caledonian tree Pycnandra acuminata produces striking blue-green latex rich in which metal?
matches.d: This hyperaccumulator can concentrate extraordinary amounts of nickel in its tissues. Nickel ions color the latex rather than an ordinary green plant pigment.

matches.q: Which part of a cell contains the chromosomes or genetic material?
Which plant fits this description? A dwarfed evergreen conifer or shrub shaped to have flat-topped asymmetrical branches and grown in a container.
matches.d: A dwarfed evergreen conifer or shrub shaped to have flat-topped asymmetrical branches and grown in a container.

candidates.q: Cardamine chenopodiifolia hedges its reproductive bets by making fruits in which two places on the same plant?
candidates.d: Its aerial fruits explode and scatter seeds. Separate underground fruits remain non-explosive and contain fewer, larger seeds, keeping some offspring near the parent’s successful site.

matches.q: Which fruit shares its Middle French name with the explosive called a grenade?
matches.d: The borrowed word literally named the fruit. Its Latin ancestry also contains a reference to seeds or grains.

matches.q: When a highway between Acapulco and Cuernavaca encountered an archaeological site, how did engineers take traffic past it without clearing the ruins?
matches.d: Sending the roadway underground allowed the archaeological remains to stay in place above the traffic.

matches.q: What can change from one growing season to another in an individual jack-in-the-pulpit as its size and resources change?
matches.d: Smaller flowering individuals tend to function as male, while larger ones can function as female. The same perennial plant can change its reproductive role over time.

matches.q: Which rainforest rodent cracks Brazil-nut pods and helps plant new trees by burying spare nuts?
matches.d: Some cached seeds remain uneaten and germinate away from the parent tree.

candidates.q: Where have researchers shown brewing yeast can spend the winter and then pass to a new insect generation?
candidates.d: Overwintering social-wasp queens carried Saccharomyces cerevisiae from autumn to spring and transmitted it to offspring. An insect gut can connect yeast populations across seasons.

matches.q: How can some fig trees penalize wasps that lay eggs without providing pollination?
matches.d: Aborting an unpollinated fig can kill the wasp offspring developing inside it. Such sanctions help keep the tree–pollinator partnership from becoming one-sided.

matches.q: Which insect has females that remain lodged inside paper wasps while their tiny adult males leave the host and fly?
matches.d: The sexes of this twisted-wing parasite lead visibly different adult lives. Parasitized wasp workers may also leave their colony.

matches.q: Which animal fits this clue? Social insect living in organized colonies; characteristically the males and fertile queen have wings during breeding season; wingless sterile females are the workers.
matches.d: Social insect living in organized colonies; characteristically the males and fertile queen have wings during breeding season; wingless sterile females are the workers. Another name is emmet.

matches.q: In the fig-wasp life cycle, which sex commonly spends its whole life inside its birth fig?
matches.d: Females leave with pollen after mating, while males remain inside.

candidates.q: In germination experiments on Suaeda aralocaspica, how did its fresh brown and black seeds differ?
candidates.a: Brown seeds were ready; black seeds were dormant
candidates.d: Brown seeds in the study were ready to germinate, while black seeds showed physiological dormancy. Producing both types spreads the risk of committing every seed to the same opportunity.

matches.q: Why did William Beal bury his long-running seed experiment in uncorked bottles with their mouths tilted downward?
matches.d: The sand-filled bottles were meant to test how long buried seeds could remain capable of germination. The downward openings kept them from becoming little water reservoirs.

matches.q: Tiny amounts of which notorious poison can help certain fire-responsive seeds germinate when released from a smoke compound?
matches.d: Researchers identified a smoke compound that slowly releases cyanide in water. In tested fire-responsive plants, this can act as a germination cue at suitable concentrations.

matches.q: Why do many tiny orchid seeds need a fungal partner to begin growing in nature?
matches.d: Unlike a bean, an orchid seed has almost no nutritional reserve. A suitable fungus can supply resources during germination, although some orchids are exceptions.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Australian tree with small flattened scales as leaves and numerous dark brown seed; valued for its timber and resin.
matches.d: Australian tree with small flattened scales as leaves and numerous dark brown seed; valued for its timber and resin. Another name is red cypress pine.

candidates.q: What can a dried-out fairy-ring champignon mushroom do when rain returns?
candidates.d: Marasmius oreades fruiting bodies can shrivel during dry weather and expand again after becoming wet. This drying-and-rehydrating behavior has earned it the nickname resurrection mushroom.

matches.q: Why can mushrooms appear to have lined themselves up in a fairy ring overnight?
matches.a: The fungus below is growing outward from a center.
matches.d: Its visible fruiting bodies can pop up around the expanding edge.

matches.q: Which genus of resurrection plants includes species that dismantle their green pigment while dry and rebuild it when water returns?
matches.d: Losing chlorophyll interrupts photosynthesis. The ability to start up again distinguishes this trick from a leaf simply dying of drought.

matches.q: What activates the small spikes in Harvard and MIT’s experimental kirigami shoe grips?
matches.d: Cuts in a thin steel sheet pop out as the sole bends. The spikes flatten again as the shoe returns toward its original shape.

matches.q: Watching which food being cooked gave Momofuku Ando the breakthrough for quick-rehydrating instant noodles?
matches.d: Hot oil drove moisture out of noodles, leaving tiny openings through which hot water could quickly return.

candidates.q: Some fungus-farming ants maintain helpful bacteria on their outer bodies. What service do those microbes provide?
candidates.d: The bacteria produce compounds that suppress fungi attacking the ants’ crop. Specialized body structures and glands help support this microbial defense.

matches.q: Leafcutter ants carry home chopped greenery largely to cultivate what underground food crop?
matches.d: The leaf pieces help support a fungus garden. These ants were practicing agriculture long before people.

matches.q: Where does the bullhorn acacia house the ants that defend it against plant-eaters?
matches.d: The tree provides nesting space plus food from nectar glands and nutrient-rich bodies. Its resident ants help defend this living home.

matches.q: Some ants housed by Cordia nodosa trees cheat their hosts by destroying which structures?
matches.d: Allomerus ants can suppress the tree’s reproduction by attacking its flowers. Castrated hosts can produce more of the swollen chambers that house the ants.

matches.q: The antibiotic compound lugdunin was discovered in bacteria living in which surprisingly ordinary human location?
matches.d: Researchers found that a nasal Staphylococcus species makes a compound that inhibits competing bacteria. The discovery came from studying our own microbial residents.

candidates.q: Leaf-cutting ants add fecal droplets to fresh leaves in their gardens. What useful material do these droplets recycle from the fungus they eat?
candidates.d: Fungal enzymes survive passage through the ants and reach newly cut leaves. They help break down plant material for the growing fungal crop.

matches.q: Which part of a hoatzin’s digestive system acts as a leaf-fermenting chamber?
matches.d: Bacteria help break down leaves before they reach the stomach.

matches.q: Leafcutter ants carry home chopped greenery largely to cultivate what underground food crop?
matches.d: The leaf pieces help support a fungus garden. These ants were practicing agriculture long before people.

matches.q: Why can canned pineapple work in a gelatin dessert when fresh pineapple prevents it setting?
matches.d: Fresh pineapple contains bromelain, which breaks gelatin proteins. The heating involved in canning disables the enzyme.

matches.q: Some fungus-farming ants maintain helpful bacteria on their outer bodies. What service do those microbes provide?
matches.d: The bacteria produce compounds that suppress fungi attacking the ants’ crop. Specialized body structures and glands help support this microbial defense.

candidates.q: Before it flowers, where is most of the tiny parasitic plant Pilostyles hidden?
candidates.d: Its vegetative body lives within the host. Small flowers and their bracts emerge through the stem surface, making the parasite suddenly visible.

matches.q: A Rafflesia can produce an enormous flower. Where has the rest of the plant been hiding?
matches.d: For much of its life this parasite is concealed in the tissues of a Tetrastigma vine.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Tropical American passion flower with finely dissected bracts; stems malodorous when crushed.
matches.d: Tropical American passion flower with finely dissected bracts; stems malodorous when crushed. Another name is love-in-a-mist.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Annual of southwestern United States cultivated for its purple flower heads and its bracts that resemble small baskets.
matches.d: Annual of southwestern United States cultivated for its purple flower heads and its bracts that resemble small baskets. Another name is Centaurea americana.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Lettuce valued especially for its edible stems.
matches.d: Lettuce valued especially for its edible stems. Another name is celtuce.

candidates.q: What human-made debris has been found tangled in Mediterranean seagrass fiber bundles called Neptune balls?
candidates.d: Wave-worked Posidonia fibers can trap pieces of plastic and carry them ashore. Researchers measured this natural trapping process in material washed onto beaches in Mallorca.

matches.q: What artificial-reef material did Hurricane Bonnie wash ashore by the thousand in North Carolina?
matches.d: Strong waves from Hurricane Bonnie in 1998 washed thousands of tires, part of an artificial reef, ashore in North Carolina.

matches.q: Which crab can be found along the coasts of the eastern Atlantic Ocean and eastern Mediterranean Sea, but not in between?
matches.d: Ocypode cursor, the tufted ghost crab, is a species of ghost crab found on sandy beaches along the coasts of the eastern Atlantic Ocean and eastern Mediterranean Sea.

matches.q: Which Alaskan fiber artist was known for her distinctive baskets made from dried fish skins?
matches.d: Frances Ann Reed was an American fiber artist and teacher based in Alaska who specialized in a distinctive style of basketry made from dried fish skins and other natural materials found in the state.

matches.q: Which term fits this clue? Artifact made by weaving or felting or knitting or crocheting natural or synthetic fibers.
matches.d: Artifact made by weaving or felting or knitting or crocheting natural or synthetic fibers. Another name is fabric.

candidates.q: In a landmark Arizona murder investigation, DNA from which overlooked plant material helped connect a vehicle to the crime scene?
candidates.d: Palo verde pods found in a truck were compared with trees near the body. The plant evidence challenged the suspect’s account of where the vehicle had been.

matches.q: An investigation into the case of Juan Rivera uncovered proof of evidence tampering when his shoes, which had the victim's blood on them, also bore DNA from what?
matches.d: An investigation into the case of Juan Rivera uncovered proof of evidence tampering when his shoes, which had the victim's blood on them, also bore DNA from the real killer.

matches.q: What familiar delivery vehicle speeds past the dentist’s office during Gill’s escape-plan scene in Finding Nemo?
matches.d: For this Pixar cameo, the place to watch is the street outside the aquarium.

matches.q: Researchers studying the nonphotosynthetic parasite Rafflesia lagascae found evidence suggesting it may have lost which entire genetic package?
matches.d: Extensive sequencing failed to find a recognizable complete plastid genome. The finding concerns that genetic package, not the loss of all DNA from the plant.

matches.q: How can the seed pods of Pisonia “birdcatcher” trees accidentally kill birds?
matches.a: Sticking to feathers until flight becomes impossible
matches.d: The sticky pods normally hitch rides on birds. Too many attached pods can entangle or weigh down the carrier; this is not evidence that the tree digests birds.

candidates.q: How does the fungus Entomophthora muscae help infected female housefly corpses spread infection to healthy males?
candidates.d: Fungal infection changes the dead female’s chemical signals. Males attracted to attempt mating can pick up infectious spores from the corpse.

matches.q: On infected yellow-eyed grasses, what are the petal-like yellow structures made by Fusarium xyrophilum actually made of?
matches.d: The fungus constructs flower lookalikes, complete with color and scent. Researchers propose that the imitation recruits insects to spread spores instead of pollen.

matches.q: In the fig-wasp life cycle, which sex commonly spends its whole life inside its birth fig?
matches.d: Females leave with pollen after mating, while males remain inside.

matches.q: The tiny eggs in a bird's nest fungus actually contain what reproductive material?
matches.d: The egglike packets, called peridioles, hold fungal spores rather than baby birds or insects.

matches.q: During courtship, what do the leg spurs of many male tarantulas hold away?
matches.d: The spurs help keep the male out of reach while mating.

candidates.q: The ants living with Nepenthes bicalcarata can do what inside the plant’s fluid-filled pitchers?
candidates.d: Camponotus schmitzi ants swim in the pitcher liquid and retrieve food. Their partnership with the carnivorous plant includes food, shelter and services that help the plant capture or process prey.

matches.q: Which microorganisms help a cobra plant break down prey captured in its pitcher?
matches.d: Bacteria living in the trap help process captured insects.

matches.q: Where does the Bornean carnivorous plant Nepenthes pudica hide many of its working pitcher traps?
matches.d: Its buried pitchers catch soil-dwelling prey. Researchers initially encountered plants that appeared to be missing the usual visible traps.

matches.q: Where does the bullhorn acacia house the ants that defend it against plant-eaters?
matches.d: The tree provides nesting space plus food from nectar glands and nutrient-rich bodies. Its resident ants help defend this living home.

matches.q: What supplies the sudden push that knocks insects from the lid of Nepenthes gracilis into its pitcher?
matches.d: Raindrop impacts make the lid oscillate. Insects on its underside can lose their grip and fall into the digestive fluid.

candidates.q: Why can temporarily ineffective, dry pitcher-plant traps eventually catch more ants than continuously slippery traps?
candidates.d: Experiments supported a model in which dry rims let scouting ants visit safely. Later wet conditions make the surface slippery when a larger recruited group arrives.

matches.q: In grip experiments, water-wrinkled fingertips let people use less force to hold which objects securely than smooth wet fingertips did?
matches.d: A study comparing dry, wet and wrinkled fingers found more efficient grip with wrinkled fingertips under wet conditions. That supports, rather than proves, a possible grip-related advantage.

matches.q: Where does the Bornean carnivorous plant Nepenthes pudica hide many of its working pitcher traps?
matches.d: Its buried pitchers catch soil-dwelling prey. Researchers initially encountered plants that appeared to be missing the usual visible traps.

matches.q: How does a musician sound the spinning bowls of Benjamin Franklin’s glass armonica?
matches.d: A foot pedal turns the glass bowls, and moistened fingertips make their rims sing.

matches.q: In which decade did “Slippery When Wet” first appear on record?
matches.d: One of its record labels is Mercury Records.

candidates.q: Why can’t ordinary seed-bank drying and freezing preserve many oak acorns?
candidates.a: They cannot tolerate that much drying
candidates.d: Such seeds are called recalcitrant. Researchers instead explore carefully prepared tissues and cryopreservation methods, because treating whole acorns like dry grain can kill them.

matches.q: The traditional Andean food chuño preserves potatoes using which natural combination?
matches.d: Potatoes are frozen, pressed to remove moisture, and dried. The method makes use of high-altitude conditions.

matches.q: Researchers regenerated a flowering Silene plant from a prehistoric squirrel cache in Siberian permafrost. What did they grow it from?
matches.d: The team cultured placental tissue from immature fruits, rather than simply germinating an ancient seed. The regenerated plants flowered and produced viable seeds.

matches.q: On infected yellow-eyed grasses, what are the petal-like yellow structures made by Fusarium xyrophilum actually made of?
matches.d: The fungus constructs flower lookalikes, complete with color and scent. Researchers propose that the imitation recruits insects to spread spores instead of pollen.

matches.q: A row of trulli in Alberobello can look like a cluster of stone hats. What shape are their roofs?
matches.d: The small limestone buildings use a traditional dry-stone construction method.

candidates.q: What unexpected growing position helped Kew propagate the tiny waterlily Nymphaea thermarum successfully?
candidates.a: On wet mud exposed to air
candidates.d: The breakthrough came from copying its hot-spring-edge habitat. Seedlings improved when kept at the surface of wet soil instead of being submerged like typical waterlily seedlings.

matches.q: For a 2025 acoustics experiment, researchers produced an orchestra-like racket by rubbing wet blades across which food?
matches.d: The blade acted like a bow, while tiny air spaces helped resonate. Their experimental bread-cheese orchestra was compared to a flock of seagulls.

matches.q: Watching which food being cooked gave Momofuku Ando the breakthrough for quick-rehydrating instant noodles?
matches.d: Hot oil drove moisture out of noodles, leaving tiny openings through which hot water could quickly return.

matches.q: Contestants at a Yukon hot spring create unusual hairstyles by letting what stiffen their wet hair?
matches.d: The winter air freezes hair above the warm pool, producing dramatic frosted shapes for photographs.

matches.q: To hide underwater, a jacana can leave only the tip of what body part exposed?
matches.d: Jacanas can remain submerged with just the bill tip above the surface.

candidates.q: The long twining part of a Lygodium climbing fern may look like a vine stem. What is it actually part of?
candidates.d: Its frond’s central axis can keep extending and coil around supports. The climbing structure is an unusually long-growing leaf rather than the main shoot of a flowering vine.

matches.q: The flowerheads of the fern-leaf spider flower, Grevillea longifolia, look like what?
matches.d: Grevillea longifolia, commonly known as fern-leaf spider flower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Proteaceae and is endemic to the Sydney Basin in New South Wales.

matches.q: Between flowering episodes, a titan arum can look like a small tree. What is that entire branching green structure botanically?
matches.d: Its single compound leaf has a tall stalk and many leaflets. That tree-like phase helps the underground storage organ build reserves.

matches.q: The long eyelashes of a hornbill are actually modified what?
matches.d: The eyelash-like structures surrounding the eyes are specialized feathers.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Rock-inhabiting fern of northern North America growing in massive tufts and having fronds resembling parsley.
matches.d: Rock-inhabiting fern of northern North America growing in massive tufts and having fronds resembling parsley. Another name is American parsley fern.

matches.q: What is the name of Nissan's most popular electric car?

candidates.q: What holds some lodgepole-pine cones shut for years until sufficient heat allows their seeds to escape?
candidates.d: In serotinous cones, resin bonds the scales together. Heat can melt that bond, releasing stored seeds after a fire has opened space for new seedlings.

matches.q: How does lodgepole pine dwarf mistletoe launch its sticky seeds toward new hosts?
matches.d: The fruit ejects its seed rapidly; the sticky coating helps the seed adhere to a new host.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Australian tree with small flattened scales as leaves and numerous dark brown seed; valued for its timber and resin.
matches.d: Australian tree with small flattened scales as leaves and numerous dark brown seed; valued for its timber and resin. Another name is red cypress pine.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Australian cypress pine having globular cones.
matches.d: Australian cypress pine having globular cones. Another name is Callitris cupressiformis.

matches.q: Which building opened in the Market Hall six years after a fire partly destroyed the building?
matches.d: The Monmouth Museum, previously known as The Nelson Museum and Local History Centre, was a museum in Monmouth, Monmouthshire, south east Wales.

candidates.q: Researchers proposed that pale patches on Caladium steudneriifolium leaves deter egg-laying moths by resembling what?
candidates.d: The variegated patches look like mines left by feeding larvae. Experiments with natural and painted markings supported the idea that appearing already attacked can discourage new attacks.

matches.q: Some passion vines bear little leaf bumps that resemble butterfly eggs. How can these decoys protect the vine?
matches.d: Some female butterflies avoid plants already carrying eggs, where their offspring would face competitors. The plant’s false eggs can exploit that preference.

matches.q: Sticky leaves of some dune plants collect a gritty coating that discourages chewing. What is the coating made of?
matches.d: Removing or adding sand in experiments changed herbivore damage. The grains form an external physical defense on plants such as Abronia latifolia.

matches.q: The pitcher plant Nepenthes ampullaria gets a substantial nutrient contribution from what falling material?
matches.d: Its pitchers collect forest leaf litter as well as other material. Isotope studies and feeding experiments support nutrition from this plant debris.

matches.q: When pollen was scarce, researchers saw bumblebees puncture leaves of nonflowering plants. What happened to the damaged plants?
matches.d: The bee damage accelerated flowering in the tested plants. Researchers’ attempts to copy the damage mechanically did not reproduce its full effect.

candidates.q: What unusual process clears away the aging gills of the mushroom Coprinus comatus as its spores mature?
candidates.d: Its cap progressively breaks down into a dark, spore-bearing fluid. Dissolving older tissue helps expose the remaining spore-producing surfaces.

matches.q: Many mushrooms launch individual spores with a microscopic catapult. What supplies the sudden kick?
matches.d: As a drop beside the spore merges with fluid on it, surface tension releases energy. High-speed filming captured the spore shooting away with the joined liquid.

matches.q: Some mushrooms can make tiny air currents to carry spores away even when the surrounding air is still. What drives these currents?
matches.d: Water evaporating from the mushroom cools nearby air. The resulting convection helps move spores beyond the crowded underside of the cap.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Common edible mushroom having an elongated shaggy white cap and black spores.
matches.d: Common edible mushroom having an elongated shaggy white cap and black spores. Another name is shaggymane.

matches.q: Why do capybaras deliberately eat some of their own droppings?
matches.d: This helps maintain the bacteria needed to process their plant-heavy diet.

candidates.q: The white patches on a typical red fly-agaric mushroom cap are leftovers from what?
candidates.a: A covering around the young mushroom
candidates.d: The universal veil surrounds the developing mushroom. As it expands, pieces of that covering can remain as patches on the cap.

matches.q: Which agaric mushroom species is found under the pines of Monterey Cypress trees and bruises pinkish-red when injured?
matches.d: Agaricus benesii is an agaric mushroom of the genus Agaricus known in English as the mull mushroom. This mushroom can be distinguished by a white cap that bruises pinkish-red when injured, a scaly lower stipe, and a conifer habitat.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Edible agaric with a soft greyish cap growing in shelving masses on dead wood.
matches.d: Edible agaric with a soft greyish cap growing in shelving masses on dead wood. Another name is oyster fungus.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Yellowish edible agaric that usually turns red when touched.
matches.d: Yellowish edible agaric that usually turns red when touched. Another name is blusher.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? Common edible mushroom having an elongated shaggy white cap and black spores.
matches.d: Common edible mushroom having an elongated shaggy white cap and black spores. Another name is shaggymane.

candidates.q: Some dramatically streaked tulips prized during Dutch tulip mania owed their patterns to what unexpected cause?
candidates.d: Tulip breaking virus can disrupt flower coloration, creating contrasting streaks. A visually prized pattern could therefore be a symptom of disease.

matches.q: ATR-16 syndrome causes very similar symptoms to ATR-X syndrome, despite being on what?
matches.d: ATR-16 syndrome, also called alpha-thalassemia-intellectual disability syndrome, is a rare disease characterized by monosomy on part of chromosome 16.

matches.q: What can infect the chestnut-blight fungus and make some infections less damaging to trees?
matches.d: Chestnut hypovirus 1 can weaken the fungus responsible for blight. It has helped control the disease in parts of Europe, although the outcome depends on local conditions.

matches.q: In Left 4 Dead, what is the name of the virus, as designated by CEDA, that causes most humans to turn into the Infected?
What disease does Ronaldo, nicknamed Gronaldo, suffer from at the end of the 2000s?
matches.d: Symptoms include drowsiness, chilliness, weight gain, pale skin, and muscle stiffness.

candidates.q: During its heat-producing flowering phase, what does a sacred lotus do when the surrounding air becomes colder?
candidates.d: The flowers can keep a relatively steady warm temperature across large environmental changes. Measurements show stronger metabolic heat output as ambient temperature falls.

matches.q: How can eastern skunk cabbage keep its flowers warm while snow remains on the ground?
matches.d: Its flower cluster can stay much warmer than the surrounding air.

matches.q: What kind of snowfall can form when cold air crosses the relatively warm, open water of a Great Lake?
matches.d: The lake supplies heat and moisture. Snow then falls downwind, sometimes in narrow bands that give nearby towns very different totals.

matches.q: An industrial vortex tube can turn a single compressed-air supply into what pair of outputs without moving machinery inside it?
matches.d: The swirling flow separates into streams at different temperatures. The compressed-air supply provides energy; the tube is not producing cooling for free.

matches.q: Besides hearing, what useful job do a bat-eared fox's oversized ears perform?
matches.d: Blood vessels in the large ears release heat to the surrounding air.

candidates.q: Bubbles can emerge from the center of a lotus leaf where water has collected. What internal process causes them?
candidates.d: A canal system sends pressurized air through leaf stalks and submerged rhizomes. Gas can vent through central leaf pores, producing visible bubbles if water covers the outlet.

matches.q: What gas is trapped under pressure inside popping candy such as Pop Rocks?
matches.d: Saliva dissolves the sugar around the pressurized bubbles, releasing the gas and producing the crackle.

matches.q: What are the car tires made of?
matches.d: A tire is designed to be mounted on the wheel rim and inflated with pressurized gas, usually air or nitrogen.

matches.q: What is the pump in the cooling system of an automobile that cause the water to circulate called?
matches.d: The pump in the cooling system of an automobile that cause the water to circulate.

matches.q: The rattling widget in a draught-style stout can helps recreate a creamy head by releasing which gas?
matches.d: Opening the can releases pressurized gas through tiny holes, creating many small bubbles.

candidates.q: Some fern colonies survive far beyond the range of the familiar leafy plants. Which living stage can make up these colonies?
candidates.d: The small sexual generation can live independently and spread vegetatively. Its distribution may extend far beyond that of the recognizable, spore-producing leafy generation.

matches.q: In many ferns, chemical signals from older reproductive plants can make nearby young gametophytes develop as what?
matches.d: The tiny gametophyte stage can respond to signals called antheridiogens. This influences sex expression before the familiar leafy fern develops.

matches.q: Which plant fits this description? The asexual spore of ferns that resembles dust; once thought to be seeds and to make the possessor invisible.
matches.d: The asexual spore of ferns that resembles dust; once thought to be seeds and to make the possessor invisible.

matches.q: What genus of bulbs in the amaryllis family is nicknamed “rain lilies” for flowers that can appear after a soaking?
matches.d: These American bulbs spread far beyond their native range as ornamentals. Their common name describes the timing gardeners watch for.

matches.q: What blacksmith’s tool gives its name to the flattened top of a thunderstorm cloud?
matches.d: The cloud top spreads horizontally. It can extend far downwind of the storm below.

candidates.q: In Charles and Francis Darwin’s grass-seedling experiments, shading which small region prevented bending toward light?
candidates.d: An opaque cap over the tip blocked the response even though the region that would bend remained exposed. The experiment separated light detection from the growth response farther down.

matches.q: Seedlings of the tropical vine studied as Monstera gigantea can find a tree to climb by growing toward what visual cue?
matches.d: A tree trunk creates a dark silhouette on the forest floor. The seedlings’ unusual growth response helps them reach a support before climbing toward better light.

matches.q: A distant road appears wet on a hot day. What is bending to create a mirage?
matches.d: Air layers at different temperatures bend light by different amounts.

matches.q: When researchers offered dodder a fake tomato plant and tomato scent on rubber, which cue guided the parasite’s growth?
matches.d: Dodder seedlings grew toward extracted plant odors even without a real host present. In choice tests they also distinguished scents from different potential hosts.

matches.q: Even though Charles P. Adams meant to hire someone else, Ralph Waldo Emerson Jones remained at Grambling what for 51 years?
matches.d: Ralph Waldo Emerson Jones Sr., known as Prez Jones, was an American educator and administrator.
